## About this manual {.unnumbered}

This document explains how to use the **DRMIS** web application (Disaster Risk Management Information System) for Vanuatu. It is written for **duty officers, analysts, field staff, and administrators** who work with hazard, exposure, and climate information.

**Typography:** This manual uses **Inter** from [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Inter) (loaded when you view or build the HTML; an internet connection is required the first time the font is fetched unless the browser has it cached).

**Screenshots:** Figures marked with a **dashed box** are *placeholder slots* — add the listed file under `docs/screenshots/` and optionally replace the slot with a normal image in the source file (`user-manual.qmd`). Existing captures are shown where files are already present.

```{=html}
<p style="font-size:0.9rem;color:#64748b;margin-top:-0.5rem;">Build HTML from this file: <code>quarto render docs/user-manual.qmd</code> — see <code>docs/README-user-manual.md</code>.</p>
```

---

# Part I — Getting started

## Introduction

DRMIS helps you to:

- Monitor **live hazard alerts** and operational indicators in the **Command Centre**.
- Explore **geospatial datasets** (tabular, vector, raster) on the **Live Map**.
- **Filter** by province, area council, year, and scenario (disaster damage, resources, financial, climate).
- **Export** data in common formats (XLSX, GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, and others where configured).
- Review **audit history** for compliance and handover.
- Manage **profile and security** in **Settings** (where your role allows).

The application has two main **workspaces**:

| Workspace | When you use it |
|-----------|-----------------|
| **Command Centre** | Dashboard, Datasets, Exports, Audit log, Settings — navigated from the left sidebar. |
| **Operations (Live Map)** | Full-screen map with left/right context panels — opened via **Live map** in the sidebar. |

## Browsers and access

- Use a **current version** of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari.
- **JavaScript** must be enabled.
- You need **network access** to the DRMIS server (or VPN if required by your organisation).
- For **browser notifications** (optional alerts), allow notifications when the app prompts you.

## Signing in

Access is **not** self-service: your administrator creates your account and credentials.

1. Open the DRMIS URL provided by your organisation.
2. Enter your **username** and **password**.
3. Click **Sign in**.

![Sign-in screen with username and password fields](screenshots/01-login_.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="DRMIS login page"}

::: {.callout-tip}
## No password reset in the app

If you cannot sign in, contact your **system administrator**. DRMIS does not offer a self-service “forgot password” flow in the user interface.
:::

# Part II — Application layout

## Main navigation (left sidebar)

The sidebar is grouped into **Operations**, **Data**, and **Governance** (labels may vary slightly by build).

| Item | Typical purpose |
|------|-----------------|
| **Dashboard** | Command Centre home — KPIs, submissions, alerts. |
| **Live map** | Interactive map and layer analysis. |
| **Datasets** | Browse dataset metadata by cluster. |
| **Exports** | Create and track data export jobs. |
| **Audit log** | Searchable history of important actions. |
| **Settings** | Profile, security, appearance (where permitted). |

Staff users may also see a link to **Django Admin** for back-office configuration.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Full shell (Dashboard)</strong><code>docs/screenshots/07-shell-overview.png</code><span class="hint">Capture the full window: DRMIS top bar, left navigation, and Command Centre main content.</span></div></div>
```

## Top bar (Command Centre)

When you are **not** on the Live Map workspace, the shell **top bar** usually includes:

- **DRMIS** branding and short system subtitle.
- **System status** indicator.
- **Alert count** (bell) — opens or reflects live alert activity.
- **Theme** toggle (light / dark).
- **Account** menu (avatar): user manual link, data entry (if allowed), share (copy link), lock screen (if PIN enabled), Django Admin (staff), **Logout**.

## Roles and what you can open

DRMIS hides menu items you are not allowed to use. Typical patterns:

| Role | Dashboard | Live map | Datasets | Exports | Audit | Settings | Data Entry (menu) |
|------|-----------|----------|----------|---------|-------|----------|-------------------|
| **Admin** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes (if enabled) |
| **Analyst** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | Yes (if enabled) |
| **Read-only** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| **Field officer** | Yes | Yes | No | No | No | No | Yes (if enabled) |

If you open a restricted URL directly, you may see **You don't have permission**.

# Part III — Command Centre (Dashboard)

## Overview

After login, the default home is the **Dashboard**. It summarises operational status and recent activity.

![Command Centre dashboard overview](screenshots/02-dashboard_.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="DRMIS dashboard with KPI cards and tables"}

### Key areas

- **KPI / metric tiles** — e.g. pending submissions, live alerts, field teams, daily updates (exact tiles depend on configuration).
- **Recent submissions** — tabular list with links for review where implemented.
- **Live alerts** — consolidated feeds (e.g. USGS, VMGD, GDACS, internal DRMIS alerts). New high-priority alerts may **pulse** the header badge and can trigger **sound** or **browser notifications** if you allowed them.
- **Risk / exposure** panels — contextual summaries where enabled.

## Creating a new incident

Where **+ New Incident** (or equivalent) is available:

1. Choose **incident type** and **severity**.
2. Select **province** and optionally **area council**.
3. Enter **title** and **summary**; attach a **photo** if required.
4. **Publish** — the incident is stored and appears in operational feeds.

Adapt steps to match the live wizard labels in your deployment.

---

# Part IV — Live Map (Operations workspace)

## Opening the Live Map

1. In the left sidebar, click **Live map**.
2. The layout switches to a **map-first** view: map stage in the centre, **context panel** on the right, **layer controls** on the left (exact widths depend on screen size).

On **small screens**, side panels may collapse into **icons** or **bottom** controls; tap to open.

## Map toolbar (floating chrome)

Above the map you will typically find:

- **Simulate** — opens the **simulation** workflow (scenario parameters and outputs depend on backend configuration).
- **Layer / scenario** controls — choose active layers and related options.
- **Legend** — explains symbols and colours for active layers.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Map floating toolbar</strong><code>docs/screenshots/08-map-floating-toolbar.png</code><span class="hint">Show Simulate, layer chip/dropdown, and Legend in one capture.</span></div></div>
```

## Scenario modes (header)

On the Live Map, the **header** lets you switch **scenario** views, for example:

- **Disaster** — baseline and disaster overlay views (damage, resources, financial) where configured.
- **Climate** — climate modules and land-cover style layers.
- **Compare** — side-by-side comparison of two years on the map.

**Keyboard shortcuts** (when the map view is active and focus is not inside a form field):

| Keys | Action |
|------|--------|
| **Alt + D** | Switch toward **Disaster** mode |
| **Alt + C** | Switch toward **Climate** mode |
| **Alt + X** | Switch toward **Compare** mode |
| **Escape** | Close certain overlays (e.g. time-series drawer) when open |

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Header scenario tabs</strong><code>docs/screenshots/10-header-mode-tabs.png</code><span class="hint">Capture Disaster / Climate / Compare (and any additional mode tabs visible).</span></div></div>
```

## Left sidebar — clusters and layers

Datasets are grouped by **cluster** (e.g. Education, Health, Logistics).  

1. Select a **cluster** from the control at the top of the left panel.
2. **Toggle** datasets to add or remove them from the map.
3. Only one **tabular** choropleth layer may be active at a time in typical configurations; **vector** and **raster** rules depend on your build.

![Left sidebar showing clusters and layer toggles](screenshots/03-left-sidebar_.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Left sidebar with dataset clusters and switches"}

### Layer ordering

Some builds allow **reordering** layers (drag handles) so that symbols draw in the correct order on top of the basemap.

## Right sidebar — area, time, and analysis lens

Use the **right sidebar** to:

- Select **one or more provinces** (multi-select).
- After provinces are chosen, narrow to **area councils** when available.
- Pick **year** for tabular data tied to a calendar year.
- Choose **data view** type for disaster overlays — e.g. **Baseline**, **Damage**, **Resources**, **Financial** (labels match your deployment).
- Apply **attribute** filters when a tabular layer is active (e.g. filter attributes or text contains).

![Right sidebar with province and analysis controls](screenshots/04-right-sidebar_.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Right sidebar filters and statistics"}

### Expanded full-width panel

To focus on charts and tables:

1. Click **expand** in the right sidebar header (icon may look like outward arrows).
2. The panel grows to use more of the screen (often overlaying the map).
3. Use **restore** to return to the split layout.

![Right sidebar expanded to full width](screenshots/05-expanded-full%20width-right-sidebar_.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Expanded right sidebar covering map area"}

## Ask the map (natural language)

If your organisation enabled the **AI map query** feature:

1. Open **Ask the map** (usually bottom-left on the Live Map).
2. Type a request in plain language, e.g. *Show schools in Tafea with more than 200 students*.
3. Press **Apply** (or **Ctrl/Cmd + Enter**).
4. The system proposes **layers, filters, and areas**; review any **warnings** shown after the run.

The assistant **does not run arbitrary SQL** — it returns a **plan** that the app applies to your existing filters and layers. If the server is not configured with an API key, the feature will show a **not configured** error.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Ask the map panel</strong><code>docs/screenshots/09-map-query-chat.png</code><span class="hint">Show the collapsed and/or expanded chat panel with an example query.</span></div></div>
```

## Compare mode

In **Compare** mode:

- Adjust **left** and **right years** using controls on the map overlay.
- Drag the **split** control to see more of one side.
- Province and layer choices still apply from the sidebars.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Compare split map</strong><code>docs/screenshots/11-compare-split-map.png</code><span class="hint">Two-year split view with legend if possible.</span></div></div>
```

## Simulation panel

**Simulate** opens a panel where you adjust scenario inputs (hazard type, intensity, assumptions — **as configured**). Use **Run** to refresh outputs and **Reset** to restore defaults.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Simulation panel</strong><code>docs/screenshots/12-simulation-panel.png</code><span class="hint">Simulation open with visible parameters and action buttons.</span></div></div>
```

## Climate view

In **Climate** mode you may see:

- **Climate modules** in the left stack (e.g. land cover, coastal — depends on data).
- **Key indicators** or storytelling widgets when a climate layer is active.
- **Raster / PMTiles** layers for specific products.

Exact names follow your administrator’s configuration.

## Legend

Open the **Legend** from the map toolbar to see:

- Active layer entries and colour scales.
- Units and labels where provided by metadata.

## Map interaction

- **Pan** by dragging; **zoom** with scroll or **+ / −** controls (if shown).
- **Click** features on the map to open **pop-ups** where implemented.
- **3D** mode, if available, is toggled from map controls — performance depends on your device.

## Save and load workspace

Use **Workspace** on the map toolbar (next to the legend) to:

- **Save current layout** — enter a name; your **layers**, **scenario** (Disaster / Climate / Compare, etc.), **cluster**, **province / area council** filters, **year**, **data view** and **climate module** selections, **map position** (center and zoom), **basemap style**, **2D/3D** mode, **compare** years and view, and **tabular** filters (where set) are stored **on the server** under your user account.

- **Load** — pick a saved layout from the list to restore it. DRMIS refetches dataset metadata for the saved cluster when possible.

- **Delete** — remove a saved layout you no longer need. A per-user limit applies (e.g. 30 slots); delete old ones to save new layouts.

Layouts are **private to your login** unless an administrator inspects them in Django Admin.

## Feedback

A **Feedback** control may appear on the map (role and build dependent). Use it to send structured comments to your operations team.

# Part V — Datasets browser

The **Datasets** page lists metadata for layers available in DRMIS, organised by **cluster** and **type** (tabular, vector, raster, etc.).

Typical actions:

1. Choose a **cluster** filter.
2. **Search** or sort the table (if available).
3. Open **detail** links to read description, source, and update dates.

Administrators may also use **Django Admin** for deep edits.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Datasets page</strong><code>docs/screenshots/13-datasets-page.png</code><span class="hint">Table of datasets with cluster filter and at least one row visible.</span></div></div>
```

# Part VI — Exports

## Export workflow

1. Go to **Exports** in the left sidebar.
2. Select a **cluster** and the **datasets** you need.
3. Choose **formats** (e.g. XLSX, GeoJSON, GeoTIFF, VRT, PMTiles — whichever your server exposes).
4. Start the export and watch **status** in the queue (spinners, success/error, toasts).

Exports honour **scope** rules defined on the server (area, year, etc.) — read on-screen hints.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Exports page</strong><code>docs/screenshots/14-exports-queue.png</code><span class="hint">Show format chips and an example job row or empty queue with call-to-action.</span></div></div>
```

## Download from the Live Map (quick export)

From the **right sidebar** on the Live Map:

1. Enable the layers you need and set **province / year** filters.
2. Open **Download Data** (or similarly labelled control).
3. In the dialog, pick **tabular (XLSX)** or **vector (GeoJSON)** (and raster links if shown).

![Download active datasets dialog](screenshots/06-download-dialog_.png){fig-align="center" width="560" fig-alt="Download dialog listing active datasets and filters"}

::: {.callout-note}
## Filtered downloads

The download uses **current map filters**. If you restrict to **Shefa** and **2024**, the file should only contain matching rows/features (subject to server rules).
:::

---

# Part VII — Audit log

1. Open **Audit log** from the sidebar.
2. **Filter** by action, date range, or free-text search as provided.
3. Change **page size** if available (e.g. 25 / 50 / 100).
4. Use **Export CSV** for offline archiving or compliance evidence.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Audit log</strong><code>docs/screenshots/15-audit-log.png</code><span class="hint">Filters + table with at least one example row.</span></div></div>
```

# Part VIII — Settings and account

## Settings page

Users with access open **Settings** from the sidebar. Tabs often include:

- **Profile** — display name, email, avatar.
- **Security** — password change, two-factor authentication (if enabled), session / lock preferences.
- **Appearance** — theme options aligned with the shell.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Settings (Profile tab)</strong><code>docs/screenshots/16-settings-profile.png</code><span class="hint">Settings page with sidebar tabs visible.</span></div></div>
```

## Account menu (top bar)

Click your **avatar** on the shell top bar to access:

- **User manual** (external or hosted copy).
- **Data Entry** (if your role allows).
- **Share** — copies the current page URL.
- **Lock screen** (if you configured a PIN).
- **Admin** (Django, staff only).
- **Logout**.

## Data Entry (field workflow)

**Data Entry** opens a dedicated workflow for **area administrators** to submit or correct local data. Fields and validation are defined by your programme. If you do not see Data Entry, your role may not include it.

```{=html}
<div class="screenshot-slot"><div class="screenshot-slot-inner"><strong>Figure — Data Entry</strong><code>docs/screenshots/17-data-entry.png</code><span class="hint">First step of the data entry flow with clear context.</span></div></div>
```

# Part IX — Reference

## Offline behaviour

If you lose connectivity, an **offline** indicator may appear. Some features require a live API; retry when the network is restored.

## URL and session tips

- Bookmark **Live map** or **Dashboard** only after login if your organisation uses SSO or short-lived sessions.
- **Deep links** (e.g. `live-map` in the path) may switch workspace automatically when the SPA loads.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to try |
|---------|-------------|
| Blank map | Reload; check VPN; confirm backend is up; try another browser. |
| Layers empty | Select a **cluster**; ensure a layer is **toggled on**; check **year** and **province** filters. |
| 403 / permission | Your role may not allow the section — contact an admin. |
| Export stuck | Wait and refresh; if persistent, contact support with job id/time. |
| Ask the map errors | Organisation may not have configured the AI backend — use manual filters. |

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Cluster** | Group of related datasets (e.g. Education, Health). |
| **Tabular** | Table data joined to admin areas (provinces / area councils) for choropleth maps. |
| **Vector** | GeoJSON features (points, lines, polygons) on the map. |
| **Raster** | Grid imagery (e.g. hazard or land cover) often via tiles. |
| **Baseline** | Non-overlay statistical view for tabular layers. |
| **Scenario** | Disaster, climate, or compare “lens” for the map header. |

## Quick reference

| Goal | Steps |
|------|--------|
| Sign in | Username + password → **Sign in** |
| Open map | Sidebar → **Live map** |
| Add layers | Left sidebar → cluster → toggle datasets |
| Filter area | Right sidebar → **Province** / **Area council** |
| Filter year | Right sidebar → **Year** |
| Disaster lens | Header → **Disaster** + **Data view** (damage / resources / financial) |
| Expand stats | Right sidebar → **Expand** full width |
| Save / load map layout | Map toolbar → **Workspace** → save or pick a saved layout |
| Export bulk | **Exports** → select datasets → run |
| Quick download | Live map → **Download Data** → choose format |
| Audit | **Audit log** → filter → **Export CSV** |
| Settings | **Settings** → Profile / Security / Appearance |
| Sign out | Avatar → **Logout** |
